cases.name: a-filter-inside-a-pool-reads-the-fields-beside-it
cases.description: Inside a pool, `want` and `wantseq` are fields of the member being built, so `dept_no == want` compares with a column, not with the word "want". The reference looked the names up among the run's, where a pool's fields no longer are once its walk is over, and refused both filters as never matching (TDC225).
cases.config: <tdc><env count="6" seed="probe" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="doc_id"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3" percent="50,30,20"/></sequence><sequence name="dkey"><gen type="formula" expr="dept_no"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="6"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="ag"><gen type="text" value="child,adult"/></sequence><switch name="want" on="ag"><case is="child"><data>1</data></case><default><gen type="text" value="2,3"/></default></switch><sequence name="wantseq"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence><sequence name="pcpA"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="dept_no == wantseq"/></sequence><sequence name="pcpB"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="dept_no == want"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}} ag=${{P.ag}} want=${{P.want}} B=${{P.pcpB.dept_no}} ws=${{P.wantseq}} A=${{P.pcpA.dept_no}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-inside-a-pool-against-a-field-that-never-matches
cases.description: The field beside the reference produces x and y, and no Docs member holds either: TDC225, naming both lists. Rust, Java and C# never checked a filter written inside a pool at all.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="probe" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="wantseq"><gen type="text" value="x,y"/></sequence><sequence name="pcpA"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="dept_no == wantseq"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}} ${{P.pcpA.dept_no}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-top-level-filter-does-not-read-another-pools-fields
cases.description: At the top level `wantseq` is no column — it is a field of Pats, which the run cannot read — so the filter compares with the word "wantseq" and can never match, as the run then refuses. The ports counted every pool's fields as the run's and let it through.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="probe" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="wantseq"><gen type="text" value="1,2"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="D"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="dept_no == wantseq"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D.dept_no}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-filter-inside-a-pool-naming-a-field-of-both-pools
cases.description: `dept_no` is a field of Docs and of Pats, the pool the reference is written in: which one is meant is not decidable (TDC232). Only the reference said so.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="probe" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2"/></sequence><sequence name="pcp"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="dept_no == 1"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-reference-inside-a-pool-to-an-undeclared-pool
cases.description: A member naming a pool that does not exist is TDC224 inside a pool as at the top level; Rust, Java and C# reported only TDC236.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="probe" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="pcp"><gen type="pool" value="Nope"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-reference-inside-a-pool-to-a-field-the-pool-has-not-got
cases.description: A qualified field the pool has not got is TDC226 inside a pool as at the top level; Rust, Java and C# passed it.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="probe" local="en"><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="pcp"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="Docs.nope == 1"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-pool-field-may-share-a-name-with-a-run-column-above-it
cases.description: A pool's fields are its own columns, so `dept_no` in Docs may share a name with the run's `dept_no`, and a filter inside Pats does not see the run's. The reference refused the pair as a duplicate (TDC032) when the run's column stood above the pool, and Python reported it as ambiguous (TDC232).
cases.config: <tdc><env count="4" seed="probe" local="en"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2"/></sequence><pool name="Docs" count="6"><sequence name="dept_no"><gen type="text" value="1,2,3"/></sequence></pool><pool name="Pats" count="4"><sequence name="pid"><gen type="increment" value="1"/></sequence><sequence name="pcp"><gen type="pool" value="Docs" filter="dept_no == 1"/></sequence></pool><sequence name="P"><gen type="pool" value="Pats" filter="pid == _count"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{P.pid}} ${{dept_no}}</data></line></block></tdc>
